sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: parse_date
tools.description: Parse a date string into an Arrow object using flexible input formats. date_string: A date string to parse, e.g. '2023-01-01' -> '2023-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'.

tools.name: get_utc_now
tools.description: Get the current time in UTC as an Arrow object. -> The current UTC time as an ISO 8601 formatted string.

tools.name: get_local_now
tools.description: Get the current time in the local timezone as an Arrow object. tz: The timezone to get the current time in. If not provided, uses the local timezone. Example: get_local_now() -> '2023-01-01T12:00:00+00:00'.

tools.name: create_arrow_now
tools.description:
Constructs an :class:`Arrow <arrow.arrow.Arrow>` object, representing "now" in the given timezone.
    
    :param tzinfo: (optional) a timezone identifier (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'UTC'). Defaults to local time.
    
    Usage::
    
        >>> create_arrow_now('Asia/Baku')
        '2019-01-24T20:26:31.146412+04:00'

tools.name: create_arrow_utc
tools.description:
Constructs an Arrow object representing the current time in UTC.
    
    Returns:
        A string representation of the Arrow object for the current UTC time.
        
    Example:
        >>> create_arrow_utc()
        '2019-01-24T16:31:40.651108+00:00'

tools.name: create_arrow_from_timestamp
tools.description:
Create an Arrow object from a Unix timestamp and optional timezone.
    
    Constructs an Arrow object from a Unix timestamp, converted to the given timezone.
    
    Args:
        timestamp: A Unix timestamp as an int, float, or string that converts to either.
        tzinfo: (optional) A timezone identifier (e.g., 'US/Eastern', 'UTC'). Defaults to local time.
        
    Returns:
        A string representation of the Arrow object.
        
    Example:
        >>> create_arrow_from_timestamp(1609459200, 'UTC')
        '2021-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'

tools.name: create_arrow_from_string
tools.description:
Constructs an Arrow object from a date string and format, in the style of datetime.strptime. Optionally replaces the parsed timezone.
    
    Args:
        date_str: The date string to parse.
        fmt: The format string using datetime format codes.
        tzinfo: (optional) A timezone expression. Defaults to the parsed timezone if fmt contains a timezone directive, otherwise UTC.
        
    Returns:
        A string representation of the created Arrow object.
        
    Example:
        >>> create_arrow_from_string('20-01-2019 15:49:10', '%d-%m-%Y %H:%M:%S')
        '2019-01-20T15:49:10+00:00'

tools.name: generate_time_range
tools.description:
Generate a range of Arrow objects between two dates at a specified interval.
    
    Args:
        frame (str): The timeframe (year, month, day, hour, minute, second)
        start (str): A datetime string in ISO format, the start of the range
        end (str, optional): A datetime string in ISO format, the end of the range
        limit (int, optional): A maximum number of results to return
    
    Returns:
        List[str]: A list of datetime strings in ISO format representing the time range
    
    Example:
        >>> generate_time_range('hour', '2023-01-01T00:00:00', '2023-01-01T03:00:00')
        ['2023-01-01T00:00:00+00:00', '2023-01-01T01:00:00+00:00', '2023-01-01T02:00:00+00:00', '2023-01-01T03:00:00+00:00']
tools.direct_call: list(arrow.arrow.Arrow.range(frame, arrow.arrow.Arrow.strptime(start, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'), arrow.arrow.Arrow.strptime(end, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ') if end is not None else None, limit=limit))

tools.name: get_time_span
tools.description: Get the start and end of a time span for a given frame. frame: The timeframe to span (year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, second). count: The number of frames to span. bounds: A string specifying whether to include or exclude start and end values ('()', '(]', '[)', or '[]'). Returns a tuple of start and end timestamps as strings.

tools.name: humanize_time_difference
tools.description:
Convert a time difference into a human-readable string.
    
    Args:
        time_diff: Time difference in seconds
        locale: Locale for the humanized string (default: "en-us")
        only_distance: If true, returns only the time difference without "in" or "ago" part
        
    Returns:
        Human-readable time difference string
        
    Example:
        >>> humanize_time_difference(-3600)
        '1 hour ago'

tools.name: extract_date_component
tools.description: Extract the date component from an Arrow object. year: The year component of the date, month: The month component of the date, day: The day component of the date, hour: The hour component of the time, minute: The minute component of the time, second: The second component of the time, microsecond: The microsecond component of the time.
tools.direct_call: arrow.arrow.Arrow(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond).date()

tools.name: get_timestamp
tools.description: Get the Unix timestamp of an Arrow object. year: The year component of the date, month: The month component of the date, day: The day component of the date, hour: The hour component of the time, minute: The minute component of the time, second: The second component of the time, microsecond: The microsecond component of the time, tzinfo: The timezone information. Example: get_timestamp(2021, 3, 15) -> 1615766400.0
tools.direct_call: arrow.arrow.Arrow(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, tzinfo).timestamp()

tools.name: get_integer_timestamp
tools.description: Get the integer Unix timestamp of an Arrow object. year: The year component of the date, month: The month component of the date, day: The day component of the date, hour: The hour component of the time, minute: The minute component of the time, second: The second component of the time, microsecond: The microsecond component of the time, tzinfo: The timezone information. Example: get_integer_timestamp(2020, 1, 1) -> 1577836800.
tools.direct_call: arrow.arrow.Arrow(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, tzinfo).int_timestamp

tools.name: clone_arrow
tools.description: Create a copy of an Arrow object. year: The year component of the Arrow object, month: The month component of the Arrow object, day: The day component of the Arrow object, hour: The hour component of the Arrow object, minute: The minute component of the Arrow object, second: The second component of the Arrow object, microsecond: The microsecond component of the Arrow object, tzinfo: The timezone info for the Arrow object. Example: clone_arrow(2023, 1, 1) -> '2023-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'.
tools.direct_call: arrow.arrow.Arrow(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, tzinfo).clone()

tools.name: format_ctime
tools.description: Format an Arrow object as a ctime string. year: The year, month: The month, day: The day, hour: The hour (optional), minute: The minute (optional), second: The second (optional), microsecond: The microsecond (optional), tzinfo: The timezone info (optional). Example: format_ctime(2019, 1, 19, 18, 26, 50) -> 'Sat Jan 19 18:26:50 2019'.
tools.direct_call: arrow.arrow.Arrow(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond, tzinfo).ctime()

tools.name: factory_parse_date
tools.description:
Parse a date string into an Arrow object using the factory method.
    
    :param date_string: A date string to parse into an Arrow object
    :param tzinfo: A timezone expression to replace the timezone
    :return: String representation of the parsed Arrow object
    
    Example:
        >>> factory_parse_date('2023-01-01', 'US/Eastern')
        '2023-01-01T00:00:00+00:00'

tools.name: factory_get_utc_now
tools.description:
Returns an :class:`Arrow <arrow.arrow.Arrow>` object, representing "now" in UTC time.
    
    Usage::
    
        >>> import arrow
        >>> arrow.utcnow()
        <Arrow [2013-05-08T05:19:07.018993+00:00]>
    
    Returns:
        A string representation of the current UTC time in Arrow format.

tools.name: factory_get_local_now
tools.description:
Returns an Arrow object representing "now" in the given timezone.
    
    :param tz: (optional) A timezone expression. Defaults to local time.
    
    Example:
        >>> factory_get_local_now()
        '2013-05-07T22:19:11.363410-07:00'
